parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing trans-specific exposure is documented: no presentation or cross-dressing offence, no facility/bathroom rule, no birth-sex custody or ward mandate, no border/document friction for foreign passports, and no trans-specific police targeting or violence record. Same-sex conduct is long lawful and the judiciary has actively protected trans interests (2017 first-instance and 2022 appellate recognition orders), evidencing functioning rule of law. Positive structural signals: implicit constitutional 'any other status' protection read to cover gender identity, 2022 statutory gender-identity workplace protection, registrable LGBTI organisations, hate-speech provisions (though gender identity coverage is unstated — an open question, not an exposure). The negatives are weak or non-trans-specific: an unsourced LGBTI-wide 'daily discrimination/violence' prevalence claim (rule 17 gives it no weight), no explicit statutory SOGI protection, religious opposition, and consultative exclusion — resident-sphere and climate signals. With no documented acceptance or working visitor-service remedy, it sits below the 0.75–0.85 tier, above the 0.55 friction tier.
